lead: Alabama plumbing has to handle humid summers, red clay, Gulf storms and the odd hard freeze. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from Huntsville to Mobile, around the clock.
risk: crawl-space pipes that freeze in cold snaps, storm flooding near the Gulf and root-damaged sewer lines in older neighborhoods
risk_short: frozen pipes, storm flooding and sewer lines
why: Many Alabama homes sit on crawl spaces, with supply lines and drains exposed under the floor. Winters are mild most years, so those pipes are often uninsulated, and a few nights in the teens can split them. Red clay soil also holds water against foundations and shifts as it dries.

Mobile and the Gulf Coast face hurricanes and heavy rain that back up sewers and flood low ground. Inland, the big older neighborhoods of Birmingham and Montgomery have aging cast-iron drains and clay sewer laterals that tree roots find easily. Rural Alabama relies heavily on septic systems.
problems: Mobile, Baldwin County and the Gulf Coast
Root intrusion in clay sewer laterals
Older parts of Birmingham and Montgomery
tips: Insulate pipes in crawl spaces and close foundation vents before a hard freeze.
Keep gutters and yard drains clear so storm water moves away from the house.
Plant trees well away from the sewer line.
Know where your main shutoff valve is before storm season.
areas: Calls come from North Alabama and the Tennessee Valley, the Birmingham metro, the Montgomery and Wiregrass areas, and the Gulf Coast.

faq.q: Do crawl-space pipes in Alabama really need insulation?
faq.a: Yes. Alabama winters are mild most years, but a few nights well below freezing can burst uninsulated pipes under the house. Pipe insulation and closed foundation vents are cheap protection, and a plumber can add heat tape to lines that freeze often.
